newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa succession vote soon, order says.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa succession vote soon, order says.

text.p: A delayed election to find a successor to Mother Teresa at the head of her Roman Catholic order will be held within the next 10 days, a spokeswoman for the Missionaries of Charity said on Monday.

"The election process is on and is likely to be completed by end-February or early next month," the spokeswoman told Reuters in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta. "The deliberations will be completed soon. Please wait for another 10 days."

The election to find a successor to the ailing 86-year-old nun has been postponed twice since last September. The first election date of September 8 was postponed because the renowned missionary was ill.

The election by secret ballot was rescheduled for February 2 after a two-week retreat, but the electoral college of the religious order decided to hold another month of deliberations first and then the election.
"Mother Teresa is better and improving. She is attending prayers and participating in deliberations," the spokeswoman added.
A senior church official said the general chapter or the electoral college might decide to reorganise the administration of the religious order, which operates in 126 countries.
"There is a possibility of various delegations of power around the world to make it easier for whoever manages the order to function," the church official said.

"This is what is done by most of the big congregations, which have a large number of members and who work in various parts of the world. It is quite possible that this model will also be introduced by the Missionaries of Charity," he said.
The official ruled out the possibility of Mother Teresa being re-elected.
"I don't think the sisters will re-elect her and impose on her great responsibilities when she is weak, feeble and sick," he added.
The 1979 Nobel Peace laureate, affectionately known as "Mother", had wanted to step down in 1990, a year after she was fitted with a heart pacemaker, but was persuaded to stay on.
She has led the order from the start, shaping the mission's work with her strong, charismatic personality. But she now wants to retire because of heart, kidney and lung problems.

Known by many as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the poor and the destitute, Mother Teresa spent three weeks in hospital last August and September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.
Two weeks later, she fell off a chair and hit her head.
She was admitted to hospital again in November to unblock two coronary arteries for the third such operation in five years.
Mother Teresa returned home shortly before Christmas after a long period of recovery delayed by bronchitis and irregular heartbeat. Her doctors have cautioned she might never be as active as before.
The election process involves the 103 members of the order's electoral order, or General Chapter. The college comprises representatives from various sections of the order's 4,500 nuns.
